</span></td>
<td id="A3.T8.5.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_r ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:2.5pt;padding-bottom:2.5pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.2.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:99.6pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_p">Logically incompatible facts that cannot simultaneously hold true within a single domain of discourse.</span>
</span></td>
<td id="A3.T8.5.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_r ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:2.5pt;padding-bottom:2.5pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.2.3.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:128.0pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T8.5.2.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Mechanism:</span> Distinct sources attribute divergent values to a functional property (single-value attribute). 
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A3.T8.5.2.3.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Impact:</span> Introduces binary logical contradictions that halt deterministic reasoning.</span>
</span></td>
<td id="A3.T8.5.2.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:2.5pt;padding-bottom:2.5pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.2.4.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:113.8pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.2.4.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T8.5.2.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Attribute Value Clash:</span> 
<br class="ltx_break">Source A: <span id="A3.T8.5.2.4.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(Newton, born_in, 1643)</span> 
<br class="ltx_break">Source B: <span id="A3.T8.5.2.4.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(Newton, born_in, 1645)</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A3.T8.5.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T8.5.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_r ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:2.5pt;padding-bottom:2.5pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.3.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:85.4pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T8.5.3.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Temporal Conflict</span></span>
</span></td>
<td id="A3.T8.5.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_r ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:2.5pt;padding-bottom:2.5pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.3.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:99.6pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.3.2.1.1" class="ltx_p">Inconsistencies arising from state changes in time-variant facts when temporal metadata is absent.</span>
</span></td>
<td id="A3.T8.5.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_r ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:2.5pt;padding-bottom:2.5pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.3.3.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:128.0pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.3.3.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T8.5.3.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Mechanism:</span> Facts valid in disjoint time intervals (<math id="A3.T8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{1}\neq T_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{1}\neq T_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>) are flattened into a static knowledge base. 
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A3.T8.5.3.3.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Impact:</span> Confuses the retriever by presenting outdated or competing truths as currently valid.</span>
</span></td>
<td id="A3.T8.5.3.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:2.5pt;padding-bottom:2.5pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.3.4.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:113.8pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.3.4.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T8.5.3.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Role Evolution:</span> 
<br class="ltx_break"><math id="A3.T8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{2020}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>2020</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{2020}</annotation></semantics></math>: <span id="A3.T8.5.3.4.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(Trump, President, USA)</span> 
<br class="ltx_break"><math id="A3.T8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{2021}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>2021</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{2021}</annotation></semantics></math>: <span id="A3.T8.5.3.4.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(Biden, President, USA)</span> 
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A3.T8.5.3.4.1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(Both retrieved without timestamps)</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A3.T8.5.4" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T8.5.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_b ltx_border_r ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:2.5pt;padding-bottom:2.5pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.4.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:85.4pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T8.5.4.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Granularity Conflict</span></span>
</span></td>
<td id="A3.T8.5.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_b ltx_border_r ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:2.5pt;padding-bottom:2.5pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.4.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:99.6pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.4.2.1.1" class="ltx_p">Discrepancies in the level of abstraction or specificity regarding the same entity or concept.</span>
</span></td>
<td id="A3.T8.5.4.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_b ltx_border_r ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:2.5pt;padding-bottom:2.5pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.4.3.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:128.0pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.4.3.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T8.5.4.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Mechanism:</span> Simultaneous mapping of an entity to hierarchically distinct nodes (e.g., specific vs. general) within an ontology. 
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A3.T8.5.4.3.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Impact:</span> Creates redundant inference paths and dilutes reasoning precision.</span>
</span></td>
<td id="A3.T8.5.4.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_b ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:2.5pt;padding-bottom:2.5pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.4.4.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:113.8pt;">
<span id="A3.T8.5.4.4.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T8.5.4.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Geospatial:</span> 
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A3.T8.5.4.4.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(Xiao Ming, born_in, Shanghai)</span> vs. <span id="A3.T8.5.4.4.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(Xiao Ming, born_in, China)</span> 
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A3.T8.5.4.4.1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Taxonomical:</span> 
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A3.T8.5.4.4.1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(AI, subclass, NLP)</span> vs. <span id="A3.T8.5.4.4.1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(AI, subclass, Machine Learning)</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Details of the Proposed Method</h2>

<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1. </span>Key Definitions</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To establish a rigorous foundation for the subsequent methodology, we first provide formal definitions for the core components of our hierarchical knowledge representation:</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">(i) <span id="A4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Type (<math id="A4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>) and Entity (<math id="A4.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>)</span>: We distinguish between abstract concepts and concrete instances. A type <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in\mathcal{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in\mathcal{T}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes a high-level taxonomic category (e.g., <span id="A4.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Person</span>) that serves as a semantic anchor. An entity <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e\in\mathcal{E}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e\in\mathcal{E}</annotation></semantics></math> refers to a specific instance grounded in the text (e.g., <span id="A4.SS1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Einstein</span>), where each entity is associated with a type through a mapping function <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi(e)=t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi(e)=t</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">(ii) <span id="A4.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Schema (<math id="A4.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>) and Fact (<math id="A4.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>)</span>: We define knowledge triples at two levels of abstraction. A schema <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s=(t_{h},r,t_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=(t_{h},r,t_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> specifies a structural constraint, where <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{h},t_{t}\in\mathcal{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{h},t_{t}\in\mathcal{T}</annotation></semantics></math> represent the head and tail types, and <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> denotes a semantic relation (e.g., (<span id="A4.SS1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Person</span>, <span id="A4.SS1.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">born_in</span>, <span id="A4.SS1.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Country</span>)). A fact <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f=(e_{h},r,e_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f=(e_{h},r,e_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> is a concrete instantiation of a schema, where <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{h},e_{t}\in\mathcal{E}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{h},e_{t}\in\mathcal{E}</annotation></semantics></math> (e.g., (<span id="A4.SS1.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Einstein</span>, <span id="A4.SS1.p3.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">born_in</span>, <span id="A4.SS1.p3.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Germany</span>)).</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">(iii) <span id="A4.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Ontology (<math id="A4.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}</annotation></semantics></math>)</span>: The ontology is defined as the structured collection of all valid schemas, denoted as <math id="A4.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}=\{s_{1},\dots,s_{n}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}=\{s_{1},\dots,s_{n}\}</annotation></semantics></math>. It governs the structural rules of the knowledge graph by enforcing semantic constraints, ensuring that all extracted facts conform to predefined schema specifications.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">(iv) <span id="A4.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Passage (<math id="A4.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>)</span>: A passage <math id="A4.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in\mathcal{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\in\mathcal{P}</annotation></semantics></math> represents a granular segment of raw text from the corpus, serving as the evidence grounding unit. Specifically, each extracted fact <math id="A4.SS1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is explicitly linked to its supporting textual evidence through a mapping function <math id="A4.SS1.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi(f)\to p_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ψ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi(f)\to p_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2. </span>MemGraphRAG architecture</h3>

<div id="A4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To overcome fragmented extraction and support the coherent evolution of knowledge graphs, we propose the MemGraphRAG architecture. Our core premise is that high-quality graph construction requires not only structured storage, but also active management of knowledge. The system is built upon two complementary components: (i) a <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Hierarchical Memory Architecture</span> that organizes schemas, facts, and passages across different abstraction levels, and (ii) a <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Multi-Agent System</span> that serves as the dynamic execution engine, leveraging memory to drive the iterative “extract–verify–modify” process. In the following sections, we describe how these components work together to ensure global consistency.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Global Memory</span>, which organizes knowledge in a three-tier structure that aligns abstract schemas, concrete facts, and supporting evidence. The top-level <span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Ontology Layer</span> (<math id="A4.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{ont}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{ont}</annotation></semantics></math>) maintains schema patterns with their statistical frequencies, providing semantic structure and global theme for graph construction. The middle <span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Fact Layer</span> (<math id="A4.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{fac}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{fac}</annotation></semantics></math>) stores instantiated triples derived from these schemas. The lowest <span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Passage Layer</span> (<math id="A4.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{pas}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{pas}</annotation></semantics></math>) preserves the original source passages, ensuring that extracted facts remain grounded in their linguistic context.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To strengthen associations across layers, we introduce a <span id="A4.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">dense indexing mechanism</span> that enforces structural consistency through bidirectional interactions. Specifically, <span id="A4.SS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Schema–Instance Alignment</span> is established not merely as a one-way classification, but as a mutual binding between abstraction and instantiation. On the bottom-up direction, we define a mapping</p>
<table id="A4.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(9)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi:\mathcal{M}_{fac}\rightarrow\mathcal{M}_{ont}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi:\mathcal{M}_{fac}\rightarrow\mathcal{M}_{ont},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">which enforces strict typing by assigning each triple <math id="A4.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in\mathcal{M}_{fac}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in\mathcal{M}_{fac}</annotation></semantics></math> to a schema constraint <math id="A4.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\in\mathcal{M}_{ont}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\in\mathcal{M}_{ont}</annotation></semantics></math>. On the top-down direction, each schema <math id="A4.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> induces its instantiation set</p>
<table id="A4.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(10)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{T}(s)=\{\,t\in\mathcal{M}_{fac}\mid\Phi(t)=s\,\},\qquad|\mathcal{T}(s)|\geq 0," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{T}(s)=\{\,t\in\mathcal{M}_{fac}\mid\Phi(t)=s\,\},\qquad|\mathcal{T}(s)|\geq 0,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.p3.3" class="ltx_p">capturing the duality that schemas constrain facts while facts substantiate schemas.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Simultaneously, <span id="A4.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Fact–Evidence Grounding</span> is modeled via a bidirectional relation</p>
<table id="A4.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(11)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi\subseteq\mathcal{M}_{fac}\times\mathcal{M}_{pas}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi\subseteq\mathcal{M}_{fac}\times\mathcal{M}_{pas},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.p4.2" class="ltx_p">which links each fact to its supporting passages (provenance) while allowing passages to index the facts they yield (extraction). For any triple <math id="A4.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, we define its evidence set as</p>
<table id="A4.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(12)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}(t)=\{\,p\in\mathcal{M}_{pas}\mid(t,p)\in\Psi\,\},\qquad|\mathcal{E}(t)|\geq 1." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}(t)=\{\,p\in\mathcal{M}_{pas}\mid(t,p)\in\Psi\,\},\qquad|\mathcal{E}(t)|\geq 1.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.p4.3" class="ltx_p">Together, these bidirectional mappings ensure that the graph is both logically governed by the ontology and rigorously grounded in textual evidence.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Hierarchical Indexing Graph</span>, which provides a unified representation spanning abstract schemas, concrete facts, and textual evidence. Concretely, we organize <math id="A4.SS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math> into three interconnected graph views that enable hierarchical navigation from high-level semantic concepts to fine-grained supporting passages. (i) <span id="A4.SS2.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Semantic Ontology Graph (<math id="A4.SS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{ont}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{ont}</annotation></semantics></math>)</span>: Derived from the ontology layer <math id="A4.SS2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{ont}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{ont}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.SS2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{ont}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{ont}</annotation></semantics></math> forms a high-level network of domain types and schema relations. It serves as the logical backbone of the overall graph by encoding valid relational patterns and domain constraints. (ii) <span id="A4.SS2.p5.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Fact Graph (<math id="A4.SS2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{fac}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{fac}</annotation></semantics></math>)</span>: Constructed from the fact layer <math id="A4.SS2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{fac}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{fac}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.SS2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{fac}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{fac}</annotation></semantics></math> represents an entity-relation graph over instantiated triples, which acts as the primary substrate for multi-hop reasoning. (iii) <span id="A4.SS2.p5.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Source Evidence Graph (<math id="A4.SS2.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{pas}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{pas}</annotation></semantics></math>)</span>: Induced from the passage layer <math id="A4.SS2.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{pas}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{pas}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.SS2.p5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{pas}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{pas}</annotation></semantics></math> grounds entities and relations in <math id="A4.SS2.p5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{fac}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{fac}</annotation></semantics></math> back to their originating text passages, providing fine-grained evidence support for faithful answer generation. Together, this multi-view architecture enables structured reasoning that progressively traverses from <math id="A4.SS2.p5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{ont}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{ont}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS2.p5.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{fac}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{fac}</annotation></semantics></math>, and finally to <math id="A4.SS2.p5.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{pas}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{pas}</annotation></semantics></math> for evidence retrieval.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Multi-Agent System</span>, which introduces the dynamic execution units that drive the system’s evolution, is formulated as a collaborative ecosystem of specialized agents interacting with <math id="A4.SS2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> through distinct cognitive roles. Specifically, the Multi-Agent System is defined as <math id="A4.SS2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}={A_{ext},A_{det},A_{res}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}={A_{ext},A_{det},A_{res}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where each agent focuses on a separate function. Our design philosophy emphasizes the decoupling of generation, diagnosis, and correction to ensure high-fidelity graph construction: (i) the <span id="A4.SS2.p6.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Extraction Agent</span> (<math id="A4.SS2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{ext}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{ext}</annotation></semantics></math>), which initializes the graph by processing input documents and populating all three layers of <math id="A4.SS2.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> (Schema, Fact, and Passage) in parallel, ensuring that each extracted fact is grounded in supporting evidence; (ii) the <span id="A4.SS2.p6.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Conflict Detection Agent</span> (<math id="A4.SS2.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{det}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{det}</annotation></semantics></math>), which is triggered by updates in the Fact Layer (<math id="A4.SS2.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}{fac}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}{fac}</annotation></semantics></math>) and performs purely diagnostic checks to identify structural anomalies, redundancy, and logical inconsistencies; and (iii) the <span id="A4.SS2.p6.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Conflict Resolution Agent</span> (<math id="A4.SS2.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A{res}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A{res}</annotation></semantics></math>), which resolves conflicts flagged by <math id="A4.SS2.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{det}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{det}</annotation></semantics></math> by leveraging the global context stored in <math id="A4.SS2.p6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math>, including historical evidence in <math id="A4.SS2.p6.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}{pas}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}{pas}</annotation></semantics></math> and schema constraints in <math id="A4.SS2.p6.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}{ont}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}{ont}</annotation></semantics></math>, thereby maintaining the global consistency of <math id="A4.SS2.p6.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="alg1" class="ltx_float ltx_float_algorithm ltx_framed ltx_framed_top">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_float"><span id="alg1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Algorithm 1</span> </span> Memory-based Indexing Graph Construction</figcaption>
<div id="alg1.4" class="ltx_listing ltx_framed ltx_framed_topbottom ltx_listing">
<div id="algx1.l1" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx1.l1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">1:</span></span>
              
              
            Document stream <math id="algx1.l1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}</annotation></semantics></math>; Global memory <math id="algx1.l1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}=\{M_{ont},M_{fac},M_{pas}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}=\{M_{ont},M_{fac},M_{pas}\}</annotation></semantics></math>;

<span id="algx1.l23.3" class="ltx_text" style="float:right;"><math id="algx1.l23.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\triangleright" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊳</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\triangleright</annotation></semantics></math> Retrieve provenance passages as evidence
</span>
</div>
<div id="algx1.l24" class="ltx_listingline">

</span>
</div>

</div>

<span id="algx1.l32.3" class="ltx_text" style="float:right;"><math id="algx1.l32.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\triangleright" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊳</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\triangleright</annotation></semantics></math> Embedding-based bridging for long-range connectivity
</span>

<section id="A4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.3. </span>Memory-based Indexing Graph Construction</h3>

<div id="A4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Traditional graph construction often processes document chunks in isolation, leading to redundant entities and fragmented subgraphs. To address this, we reframe graph construction not as a one-off extraction task, but as a <span id="A4.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">dynamic co-evolution process</span> between the Global Memory <math id="A4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> and the Knowledge Graph <math id="A4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Driven by the memory system, we implement two strategic paradigms to ensure structural integrity:
(i) <span id="A4.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Structure Optimization via Progressive Construction</span>: Instead of trusting LLM outputs immediately, we treat extractions as hypotheses. The memory acts as a “probationary sandbox,” allowing the graph to evolve via an iterative “extract–verify–modify” cycle that filters noise before it pollutes the graph structure.
(ii) <span id="A4.SS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Conflict Resolution via Global Perspective</span>: By maintaining a persistent global state, our shared memory enables the system to detect and resolve semantic contradictions (e.g., logical, temporal, or granular conflicts) that span across disparate documents, ensuring a unified and consistent knowledge representation.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS3.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.3.1. </span>Thematic Denoising via Unified Schema Filtering</h4>

<div id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To mitigate the stochastic hallucinations inherent in LLMs and ensure statistical consensus, we implement a <span id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">“Probationary Extraction Protocol.”</span> This protocol enforces a strict separation between raw extractions and validated knowledge.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">First, Composite Extraction into Memory.</span>
The process initiates by partitioning the document stream into uniform chunks <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{i}\in\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{i}\in\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math>. For each chunk, the Extraction Agent (<math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{ext}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{ext}</annotation></semantics></math>) generates a <span id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Composite Extraction Record</span> that simultaneously populates all three memory layers:</p>
<table id="A4.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(13)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{ext}(c_{i})\rightarrow\{O_{\text{cand}},T_{\text{cand}},P_{\text{src}}\}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mtext>cand</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext>cand</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>src</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{ext}(c_{i})\rightarrow\{O_{\text{cand}},T_{\text{cand}},P_{\text{src}}\}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O_{\text{cand}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>O</mi><mtext>cand</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O_{\text{cand}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\text{cand}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext>cand</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\text{cand}}</annotation></semantics></math> represent candidate schemas and triples, and <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{src}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>src</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\text{src}}</annotation></semantics></math> anchors them to the source text.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Second, The Ontology Filter Mechanism.</span>
Crucially, newly extracted schemas are initially assigned a logical “Candidate State” (Pending). While physically stored in memory for tracking, they remain <span id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">invisible</span> to the global graph structure <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math>. This isolation prevents low-frequency noise from polluting the index.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Finally, Confidence-Driven State Promotion.</span>
We formalize the evolution of knowledge using a frequency-based confidence function. A schema transitions from “Pending” to “Stable” only when its extraction frequency across the corpus exceeds a statistical threshold <math id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A4.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(14)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{State}(o)=\begin{cases}\texttt{Stable},&amp;\text{if }\mathrm{Freq}(o)\geq\tau,\\[6.0pt]
\texttt{Pending},&amp;\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>State</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>o</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">Stable</mtext><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mtext>if </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Freq</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>o</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">Pending</mtext><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext>otherwise</mtext><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{State}(o)=\begin{cases}\texttt{Stable},&amp;\text{if }\mathrm{Freq}(o)\geq\tau,\\[6.0pt]
\texttt{Pending},&amp;\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">This transition triggers a <span id="A4.SS3.SSS1.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">cascading activation</span>: only triples governed by a stable schema are flagged as “Active.” Only these active triples are permitted to enter the subsequent conflict detection phase, ensuring the graph is constructed solely from consensus-verified knowledge.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS3.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.3.2. </span>Consistency Maintenance via Global Adjudication</h4>

<div id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Dynamic graph updates inevitably introduce contradictions. To ensure trustworthiness, we implement a collaborative mechanism where agents utilize Global Memory as the “ground truth” for adjudication.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Step 1: Asynchronous Conflict Triggering.</span>
The Conflict Detection Agent (<math id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{det}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{det}</annotation></semantics></math>) is triggered strictly when a triple <math id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\text{new}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mtext>new</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\text{new}}</annotation></semantics></math> transitions to an “Active” state. <math id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{det}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{det}</annotation></semantics></math> performs a hybrid scan over the existing Fact Memory (<math id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{\text{fac}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mtext>fac</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{\text{fac}}</annotation></semantics></math>), utilizing both vector similarity and symbolic matching to identify potential conflict candidates <math id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\text{conf}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext>conf</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\text{conf}}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A4.E15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(15)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\mathrm{conf}}=\left\{t^{\prime}\in\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{fac}}\;\middle|\;\mathrm{Sim}(t_{\mathrm{new}},t^{\prime})&gt;\delta\;\lor\;\mathrm{Match}(t_{\mathrm{new}},t^{\prime})\right\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>conf</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>fac</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Sim</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>new</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0.502em" rspace="0.502em">∨</mo><mrow><mi>Match</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>new</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\mathrm{conf}}=\left\{t^{\prime}\in\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{fac}}\;\middle|\;\mathrm{Sim}(t_{\mathrm{new}},t^{\prime})&gt;\delta\;\lor\;\mathrm{Match}(t_{\mathrm{new}},t^{\prime})\right\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">If <math id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\mathrm{conf}}\neq\emptyset" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>conf</mi></msub><mo>≠</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\mathrm{conf}}\neq\emptyset</annotation></semantics></math>, the resolution protocol is initiated.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Step 2: Evidence Retrieval and Adjudication.</span>
Unlike black-box resolution, our approach is evidence-driven. The Conflict Resolution Agent (<math id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{res}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{res}</annotation></semantics></math>) leverages the memory mapping <math id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi</annotation></semantics></math> to retrieve the original provenance for both the new assertion and the conflicting facts. It constructs a context window <math id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\text{ctx}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mtext>ctx</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\text{ctx}}</annotation></semantics></math> containing the raw source passages:</p>
<table id="A4.E16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(16)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\mathrm{ctx}}=\Psi(t_{\mathrm{new}})\cup\bigcup_{t^{\prime}\in T_{\mathrm{conf}}}\Psi(t^{\prime})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>ctx</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>new</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">∪</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">⋃</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>conf</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\mathrm{ctx}}=\Psi(t_{\mathrm{new}})\cup\bigcup_{t^{\prime}\in T_{\mathrm{conf}}}\Psi(t^{\prime}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">Based on <math id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\text{ctx}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mtext>ctx</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\text{ctx}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{res}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{res}</annotation></semantics></math> reasons to determine factual validity, effectively acting as a judge reviewing case files.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Step 3: Taxonomy-Based Resolution Strategies.</span>
Based on the evidence, <math id="A4.SS3.SSS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{res}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{res}</annotation></semantics></math> executes targeted updates to resolve specific conflict types:</p>
<ul id="A4.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Mutually Exclusive Conflict (Logical):</span> For contradictory facts (e.g., conflicting birthplaces), the agent compares evidence reliability to discard the erroneous fact.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Temporal Conflict:</span> For facts valid in different periods (e.g., distinct presidential terms), the agent resolves ambiguity by appending temporal attributes (e.g., adding “46th” vs. “47th”).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Granularity Conflict (Structural):</span> For facts describing the same reality at different abstraction levels (e.g., “Shanghai” vs. “China”), the agent refines predicates to allow logical coexistence (e.g., <span id="A4.I1.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">born_city</span> vs. <span id="A4.I1.i3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">born_country</span>).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS3.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.3.3. </span>Structural Unification via Memory-Guided Bridging</h4>

<div id="A4.SS3.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The final phase transforms the validated contents of the memory system into a navigable Global Hierarchical Graph <math id="A4.SS3.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math>. We adopt a <span id="A4.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">multi-view projection strategy</span> that maps the three memory layers into corresponding graph views: <math id="A4.SS3.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{ont}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{ont}</annotation></semantics></math> (Schema View), <math id="A4.SS3.SSS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{fac}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{fac}</annotation></semantics></math> (Fact View), and <math id="A4.SS3.SSS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{pas}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{pas}</annotation></semantics></math> (Source View).</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS3.SSS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To address the common issue of disjoint subgraphs in extracted knowledge, we augment the primary reasoning substrate, <math id="A4.SS3.SSS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{fac}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{fac}</annotation></semantics></math>, with two <span id="A4.SS3.SSS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">memory-enabled connectivity mechanisms</span>:</p>
<ol id="A4.I2" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A4.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(1)</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Type-Based Bridging:</span> Leveraging <math id="A4.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{ont}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{ont}</annotation></semantics></math>, disjoint entities are explicitly connected if they map to the same high-level schema type (e.g., connecting all <span id="A4.I2.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Researchers</span> regardless of their document origin).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(2)</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Similarity-Based Bridging:</span> Leveraging embedding storage in <math id="A4.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math>, we introduce implicit edges between entity pairs whose vector similarity exceeds a threshold <math id="A4.I2.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">These mechanisms leverage the global nature of memory to connect long-distance entities, significantly enhancing the graph’s ability to support multi-hop reasoning across documents where explicit textual links are missing.</p>
</div>
<figure id="alg2" class="ltx_float ltx_float_algorithm ltx_framed ltx_framed_top">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_float"><span id="alg2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Algorithm 2</span> </span> Memory-guided Online Retrieval</figcaption>
<div id="alg2.4" class="ltx_listing ltx_framed ltx_framed_topbottom ltx_listing">
<div id="algx2.l1" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">1:</span></span>
                
                
              Query embedding <math id="algx2.l1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐪</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{q}</annotation></semantics></math>; Graph <math id="algx2.l1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math> with transition matrix <math id="algx2.l1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐌</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{M}</annotation></semantics></math>;
Memory <math id="algx2.l1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}=\{M_{ont},M_{fac},M_{pas}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}=\{M_{ont},M_{fac},M_{pas}\}</annotation></semantics></math>;
top-<math id="algx2.l1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>; threshold <math id="algx2.l1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>; damping <math id="algx2.l1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math>; balance <math id="algx2.l1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="algx2.l2" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">2:</span></span>
                
                
              Evidence set <math id="algx2.l2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math> for downstream LLM generation

</div>
<div id="algx2.l3" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">3:</span></span>
                
                
              <span id="algx2.l3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Stage I: Multi-layer Retrieval and Filtering</span>

</div>
<div id="algx2.l4" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">4:</span></span>
                
                
              <math id="algx2.l4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{raw}\leftarrow\textsc{TopK}(M_{ont},\mathbf{q},K)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">TopK</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐪</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{raw}\leftarrow\textsc{TopK}(M_{ont},\mathbf{q},K)</annotation></semantics></math>;
