                <math id="algx2.l17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{p}^{(k+1)}\leftarrow(1-\lambda)\mathbf{M}\mathbf{p}^{(k)}+\lambda\mathbf{p}^{(0)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐩</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐌𝐩</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐩</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{p}^{(k+1)}\leftarrow(1-\lambda)\mathbf{M}\mathbf{p}^{(k)}+\lambda\mathbf{p}^{(0)}</annotation></semantics></math>
<span id="algx2.l17.3" class="ltx_text" style="float:right;"><math id="algx2.l17.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\triangleright" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊳</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\triangleright</annotation></semantics></math> Personalized PageRank with restart
</span>
</div>
<div id="algx2.l18" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l18.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">18:</span></span>
                
                
              <span id="algx2.l18.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">until</span> convergence

</div>
<div id="algx2.l19" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l19.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">19:</span></span>
                
                
              Select top-ranked passages <math id="algx2.l19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> and entities <math id="algx2.l19.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="algx2.l19.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{p}^{(\infty)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐩</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{p}^{(\infty)}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="algx2.l20" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l20.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">20:</span></span>
                
                
              <math id="algx2.l20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}\leftarrow\mathcal{P}^{*}\cup\mathcal{E}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∪</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}\leftarrow\mathcal{P}^{*}\cup\mathcal{E}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="algx2.l21" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algx2.l21.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">21:</span></span>
                
                
              <span id="algx2.l21.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">return</span> <math id="algx2.l21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
</div>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Prompt Set</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To provide a more intuitive illustration of our graph construction procedure and ensure reproducibility, we present the <span id="A5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Conflict Detection</span> and <span id="A5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Conflict Resolution</span> components used in MemGraphRAG indexing, as shown in Figure <a href="#A5.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Appendix E Prompt Set ‣ MemGraphRAG: Memory-based Multi-Agent System for Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> and  <a href="#A5.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Appendix E Prompt Set ‣ MemGraphRAG: Memory-based Multi-Agent System for Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F7" class="ltx_figure"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A5.F7.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="986.41" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 477.38 986.41" width="477.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,986.41) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#808080;--ltx-fill-color:#808080;--ltx-fg-color:#808080;" color="#808080" fill="#808080" fill-opacity="0.5" stroke="#808080" stroke-opacity="0.5"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 3.54 -3.54 L 3.54 982.86 L 480.92 982.86 L 480.92 -3.54 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#6E78BE;" fill="#6E78BE" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 986.41 L 477.38 986.41 L 477.38 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 5.91 5.91 L 5.91 952.89 L 471.47 952.89 L 471.47 5.91 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 962.73)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:18.94em;--ltx-fo-height:1em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:10pt;" height="13.84" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 13.84)" width="262.08"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A5.F7.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:18.94em;">
<span id="A5.F7.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.F7.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:144%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">Conflict Detection</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 17.72)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:29.88em;--ltx-fo-height:66.73em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:10pt;" height="923.37" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 923.37)" width="413.46"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A5.F7.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:29.88em;">
<span id="A5.F7.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.F7.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Task Definitions:<span id="A5.F7.pic1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> You are an expert fact checker. Given a target triple and a list of related triples. Your task: Detect whether target triple conflicts with any triple in the list of related triples, and classify conflicts into three types:
</span></span></span>
<span id="A5.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<span id="A5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">mutual conflict (mutual exclusivity / one-to-one relations)
</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Temporal conflict (time-dependent facts; conflicts arise when time scopes overlap or are missing)
</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A5.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Granularity conflict (different levels of specificity; may be compatible via containment)
</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A5.F7.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.F7.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Definitions and rules:
</span></span>
<span id="A5.F7.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.F7.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">1. mutual conflict (type = ‘‘mutual")<span id="A5.F7.pic1.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
A mutual conflict happens when:
</span></span></span>
<span id="A5.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<span id="A5.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Same subject and predicate, but different objects, AND the predicate is one-to-one / mutually exclusive. Example: (X, birthplace, Shanghai) vs (X, birthplace, Beijing)
</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A5.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Or cyclic/contradictory relational structure that cannot both be true under common-sense constraints. Example: (A, father, B) vs (B, father, A)
</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A5.F7.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.F7.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">2. Temporal conflict (type = ‘‘temporal")<span id="A5.F7.pic1.2.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
A temporal conflict happens when:
</span></span></span>
<span id="A5.I3" class="ltx_itemize">
<span id="A5.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I3.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The predicate describes a role/state that can change over time and is typically unique at a given moment
(e.g., president/CEO/champion/current location).
</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A5.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I3.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If both triples claim different objects for the same subject-predicate:
</span></span>
<span id="A5.I3.i2.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<span id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">–</span></span> 
<span id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If explicit time scopes exist and overlap </span><math id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> hard temporal conflict.
</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">–</span></span> 
<span id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If time scopes exist and do NOT overlap </span><math id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> not a conflict.
</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">–</span></span> 
<span id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If time scopes are missing but the predicate is time-variant and moment-unique </span><math id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A5.I3.i2.I1.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> suspected temporal conflict
(ask for time ranges; do NOT assert a hard conflict without time info).
</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A5.F7.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.F7.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">3. Granularity conflict (type = ‘‘granularity")<span id="A5.F7.pic1.2.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
</span></span></span>
<span id="A5.I4" class="ltx_itemize">
<span id="A5.I4.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I4.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I4.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I4.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Triples differ due to specificity/abstraction level.</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A5.I4.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Example: (X, birthplace, Shanghai) vs (X, birthplace, China)
</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A5.I4.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I4.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I4.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I4.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If one object is a parent/superset/contains the other (hypernym/meronym/administrative containment), then it is usually compatible </span><math id="A5.I4.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A5.I4.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> classify as "granularity".
</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A5.I4.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I4.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I4.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I4.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If objects are incompatible (cannot contain each other and cannot both be true) </span><math id="A5.I4.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A5.I4.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> Logical conflict.
</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A5.F7.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.F7.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Output MUST be a valid JSON object following the required schema.
</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>. </span><span id="A5.F7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">The prompt used for Conflict Detection Agent.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A5.F8" class="ltx_figure"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A5.F8.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="768.35" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 477.38 768.35" width="477.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,768.35) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#808080;--ltx-fill-color:#808080;--ltx-fg-color:#808080;" color="#808080" fill="#808080" fill-opacity="0.5" stroke="#808080" stroke-opacity="0.5"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 3.54 -3.54 L 3.54 764.81 L 480.92 764.81 L 480.92 -3.54 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#78C378;" fill="#78C378" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 768.35 L 477.38 768.35 L 477.38 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FFFFFF;" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 5.91 5.91 L 5.91 734.83 L 471.47 734.83 L 471.47 5.91 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 744.67)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:18.94em;--ltx-fo-height:1em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:10pt;" height="13.84" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 13.84)" width="262.08"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A5.F8.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:18.94em;">
<span id="A5.F8.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.F8.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:144%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">Conflict Resolution</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 17.72)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:29.88em;--ltx-fo-height:50.97em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:10pt;" height="705.31" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 705.31)" width="413.46"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A5.F8.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:29.88em;">
<span id="A5.F8.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.F8.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Task Definitions:<span id="A5.F8.pic1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> You are an expert knowledge graph curator. Given a set of conflicting triples and their source passages, your task is to resolve the conflicts and produce corrected triples.
</span></span></span>
<span id="A5.F8.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.F8.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Conflict Resolution Strategies:<span id="A5.F8.pic1.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
</span></span></span>
<span id="A5.F8.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.F8.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">1. Mutual Conflict (type = ‘‘mutual"):<span id="A5.F8.pic1.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> These are contradictory claims about the same entity (e.g., same subject-predicate but different objects)
</span></span></span>
<span id="A5.I5" class="ltx_itemize">
<span id="A5.I5.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I5.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I5.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I5.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Resolution: Analyze the source passages to determine which triple is more accurate
</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A5.I5.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I5.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I5.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I5.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Keep only the CORRECT triple, discard the incorrect one(s)
</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A5.I5.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I5.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I5.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I5.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If both seem equally valid based on context, prefer the one with more specific/credible source
</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A5.F8.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.F8.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">2. Temporal Conflict (type = ‘‘temporal"):<span id="A5.F8.pic1.2.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> These are time-dependent facts where time scopes overlap or are missing
</span></span></span>
<span id="A5.I6" class="ltx_itemize">
<span id="A5.I6.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I6.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I6.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I6.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Resolution: Add time information to the relation to distinguish the facts
</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A5.I6.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I6.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I6.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I6.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Modify the predicate to include time context (e.g., "was president of [2000-2005]" vs "was president of [2005-2010]")
</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A5.I6.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I6.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I6.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I6.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If time info is not in sources, note it as ‘‘temporal_conflict_unresolved"
</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A5.F8.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.F8.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">3. Granularity Conflict (type = ‘‘granularity"):<span id="A5.F8.pic1.2.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> These are facts at different levels of specificity (e.g., "born in Shanghai" vs "born in China")
</span></span></span>
<span id="A5.I7" class="ltx_itemize">
<span id="A5.I7.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I7.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I7.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I7.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Resolution: Add granularity description to the relation to clarify the scope
</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A5.I7.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I7.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I7.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I7.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Modify the predicate to include granularity context (e.g., "was born in [city: Shanghai]" vs "was born in [country: China]")
</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A5.I7.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A5.I7.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A5.I7.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I7.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Both can be kept if they are compatible (containment relationship)
</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A5.F8.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.F8.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Output MUST be a valid JSON object following the required schema.
</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F8.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 8</span>. </span><span id="A5.F8.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">The prompt used for Conflict Resolution Agent.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.1. </span>Memory-guided Online Retrieval</h3>

<div id="A5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Building upon the constructed Global Hierarchical Graph <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math> and the Global Memory <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math>, this section details our memory-guided retrieval and reasoning mechanism. To bridge the gap between the user query and the complex graph topology, the inference workflow unfolds through three logically progressive stages: The workflow consists of three key steps: i) <span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Multi-Layer Memory Retrieval</span>, which retrieves initial initial candidate evidence, including schemas <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>, facts <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>, and passages <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{ont}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{ont}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{fac}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{fac}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{pas}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{pas}</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively. It then applies a preliminary noise filtering process to ensure relevance. ii) <span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Structure-Aware Node Initialization</span>, which projects the retrieved evidence onto the graph structure by mapping them to initial node weights. We apply distinct scoring strategies for Entity nodes <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>, Type nodes <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, and Passage nodes <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>, integrating semantic relevance, topological constraints, and information density. iii) <span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Graph Propagation</span>, which executes the Personalized PageRank (PPR) algorithm on the heterogeneous graph, initiating from the weighted nodes. This propagation diffuses importance across the graph to identify the most globally significant passages and nodes, which are then selected for downstream LLM generation.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">E.1.1. </span>Multi-Layer Memory Filtering</h4>

<div id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The retrieval phase initiates by querying the three distinct layers of the Global Memory<math id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> in parallel. Given a user query <math id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐪</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{q}</annotation></semantics></math>, we parallelly retrieve top-<math id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> candidates from <math id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{ont}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{ont}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{fac}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{fac}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{pas}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{pas}</annotation></semantics></math> respectively. To prevent low-relevance noise from propagating into the graph reasoning stage, we apply a strict relevance filter. For the retrieved schemas <math id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{ret}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{ret}</annotation></semantics></math> and facts <math id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{F}_{ret}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{F}_{ret}</annotation></semantics></math>, only candidates satisfying a semantic similarity threshold <math id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{Sim}(\mathbf{q},\mathbf{x})&gt;\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>Sim</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐪</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Sim}(\mathbf{q},\mathbf{x})&gt;\tau</annotation></semantics></math> are retained. This filtering ensures that the subsequent node initialization is seeded exclusively with high-confidence structural evidence. Crucially, to guarantee system robustness, if the filtering process yields no valid structural evidence (i.e., <math id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{\mathrm{ret}}\cup F_{\mathrm{ret}}=\emptyset" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>ret</mi></msub><mo>∪</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>ret</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{\mathrm{ret}}\cup F_{\mathrm{ret}}=\emptyset</annotation></semantics></math>), the framework adaptively falls back to a standard RAG mode, relying solely on the direct similarity between the query and the content in <math id="A5.SS1.SSS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{pas}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{pas}</annotation></semantics></math> for answer generation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">E.1.2. </span>Structure-Aware Node Initialization</h4>

<div id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To seed the subsequent graph propagation process with specific semantic context, we must project the retrieved evidence onto the heterogeneous graph topology. Formally, we define an initial reset probability distribution <math id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{init}(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{init}(v)</annotation></semantics></math> for any node <math id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v\in\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v\in\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math>. This distribution provides an initial importance score for the inference algorithm, quantifying the intrinsic significance of each node prior to information diffusion.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1. Entity Node Initialization via Facts:</span> To ensure that graph propagation originates from grounded evidence, we first initialize entity nodes based on the relevance of their associated facts retrieved from <math id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{fac}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{fac}</annotation></semantics></math>. Formally, we quantify the initial importance of an entity e as the mean semantic similarity of all filtered facts containing it:</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<table id="A5.E17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(17)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.E17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{init}(e)=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{F}_{e}|}\sum_{f\in\mathcal{F}_{e}}\text{Sim}(\mathbf{q},\mathbf{f})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mrow><mtext>Sim</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐪</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐟</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{init}(e)=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{F}_{e}|}\sum_{f\in\mathcal{F}_{e}}\text{Sim}(\mathbf{q},\mathbf{f})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{F}_{e}\subseteq\mathcal{F}_{ret}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>⊆</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{F}_{e}\subseteq\mathcal{F}_{ret}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the subset of query-relevant facts contain entity <math id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math>. If <math id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{F}_{e}=\emptyset" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{F}_{e}=\emptyset</annotation></semantics></math>, the weight defaults to 0. This aggregation strategy ensures that entities are activated strictly by explicit, query-relevant factual support.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">2. Type Node Initialization via Schemas:</span> To incorporate macro-level domain knowledge and avoid introducing irrelevant semantics, we further initialize type nodes <math id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in\mathcal{G}_{\text{schema}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mtext>schema</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in\mathcal{G}_{\text{schema}}</annotation></semantics></math> based on the retrieved schemas from <math id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{\text{ont}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mtext>ont</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{\text{ont}}</annotation></semantics></math>. A critical challenge is that type nodes often exhibit disproportionately large degrees (e.g., a generic “Person” node connected to thousands of entities). Activating such high-degree nodes directly would cause importance to diffuse too broadly across the graph, thereby introducing substantial noise. To address this issue, we introduce a structural regularization term that combines semantic relevance with a log-degree penalty:</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<table id="A5.E18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(18)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.E18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{init}(t)=\underbrace{\left(\frac{1}{|\mathcal{S}_{t}|}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}_{t}}\text{Sim}(\mathbf{q},\mathbf{s})\right)}_{\text{Schema Relevance}}\times\underbrace{\frac{1}{\log(\text{deg}(t)+1)}}_{\text{Hub Suppression}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mrow><mtext>Sim</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐪</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐬</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>Schema Relevance</mtext></munder><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mtext>deg</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>Hub Suppression</mtext></munder></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{init}(t)=\underbrace{\left(\frac{1}{|\mathcal{S}_{t}|}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}_{t}}\text{Sim}(\mathbf{q},\mathbf{s})\right)}_{\text{Schema Relevance}}\times\underbrace{\frac{1}{\log(\text{deg}(t)+1)}}_{\text{Hub Suppression}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p7.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the subset of retrieved schemas corresponding to type <math id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{deg}(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>deg</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{deg}(t)</annotation></semantics></math> is the node degree. This formulation effectively leverages ontology as a weak supervision signal while strictly constraining the diffusion radius of overly generic concepts.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">3. Passage Initialization with Information Density:</span> Finally, we need to initialize the Passage Nodes (<math id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in G_{pas}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>G</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\in G_{pas}</annotation></semantics></math>). We formulate the comprehensive scoring function to prioritize semantically relevant sources with high-value information, while avoiding dominance over finer-grained entity nodes, as follows:</p>
<table id="A5.E19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(19)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.E19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{init}(p)=\text{Sim}(\mathbf{q},\mathbf{d}_{p})\times\alpha\times\underbrace{\sigma\left(\frac{\sum_{e\in\mathcal{E}_{p}}\text{IDF}(e)}{\log(|\mathcal{E}_{p}|+1)}\right)}_{\text{Information Density Term}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mtext>Sim</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐪</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐝</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mrow><mtext>IDF</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>Information Density Term</mtext></munder></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{init}(p)=\text{Sim}(\mathbf{q},\mathbf{d}_{p})\times\alpha\times\underbrace{\sigma\left(\frac{\sum_{e\in\mathcal{E}_{p}}\text{IDF}(e)}{\log(|\mathcal{E}_{p}|+1)}\right)}_{\text{Information Density Term}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p8.2" class="ltx_p">This formula integrates three critical dimensions: (i) <span id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p8.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Semantic Alignment</span> (<span id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p8.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath">Sim</span>), which measures the vector similarity between the query <math id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> and the passage embedding <math id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>; (ii) <span id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p8.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Structural Balance</span> (<math id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>), a dampening coefficient empirically set to 0.05, which prevents dense passage nodes from overwhelming sparse entity nodes during the initial propagation phase and ensures a balanced importance distribution; and (iii) <span id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p8.2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Information Density Term</span>, which quantifies content quality by summing the Inverse Document Frequency (IDF) of entities <math id="A5.SS1.SSS2.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> within the passage and applying log-normalization, thereby rewarding passages that contain rare and discriminative facts rather than generic, verbose content.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS1.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">E.1.3. </span>Personalized PageRank</h4>

<div id="A5.SS1.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following the initialization phase, We execute the Personalized PageRank (PPR) algorithm on the heterogeneous graph to diffuse the initial semantic energy. The propagation uses the normalized vector <math id="A5.SS1.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{p}^{(0)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐩</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{p}^{(0)}</annotation></semantics></math> as the starting distribution and follows the iteration:</p>
<table id="A5.E20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(20)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.E20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}^{(k+1)}=(1-\lambda)\mathbf{W}\mathbf{v}^{(k)}+\lambda\mathbf{v}^{(0)}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐯</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐖𝐯</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐯</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}^{(k+1)}=(1-\lambda)\mathbf{W}\mathbf{v}^{(k)}+\lambda\mathbf{v}^{(0)}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A5.SS1.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐖</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}</annotation></semantics></math> is the transition matrix of the graph. We specifically set the damping factor <math id="A5.SS1.SSS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda=0.5</annotation></semantics></math> to restrict the random walk to a local neighborhood, thereby preventing semantic drift into irrelevant multi-hop connections. Upon convergence to <math id="A5.SS1.SSS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}^{(\infty)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐯</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}^{(\infty)}</annotation></semantics></math> the top-K passages and top-M entities with the highest scores are selected as the context window for LLM inference.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Benchmark Dataset</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first evaluate the effectiveness of MemGraphRAG on three widely-used multi-hop QA datasets, including HotpotQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2018</a>)</cite>, 2WikiMultiHopQA (2Wiki) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ho et al., 2020</a>)</cite> and MuSiQue <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Trivedi et al., 2022</a>)</cite> and two GraphRAG benchmarks: G-bench (Novel) and G-bench (Medical) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xiang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. We provide a concise overview of each dataset’s key characteristics below.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(i) HotpotQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2018</a>)</cite>:</span> A widely adopted dataset for evaluating multi-hop reasoning across disparate texts. It requires models to filter through distractor paragraphs and synthesize information from multiple supporting documents to answer complex queries, thereby testing the system’s ability to perform effective cross-document evidence retrieval.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(ii) 2WikiMultiHopQA (2Wiki) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ho et al., 2020</a>)</cite>:</span> A benchmark derived from Wikipedia knowledge graphs, specifically constructed to test structured reasoning. It consists of queries that necessitate aggregating evidence chains from two to four specific articles, focusing on the model’s capacity to handle complex entity relationships and maintain logical consistency.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(iii) MuSiQue <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Trivedi et al., 2022</a>)</cite>:</span> A challenging dataset designed to minimize reasoning shortcuts often found in earlier benchmarks. It features connected reasoning chains of 2-4 hops, requiring systems to perform strictly sequential logical inference across multiple documents to derive the correct answer.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(iv) G-bench (Novel) &amp; G-bench (Medical)</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xiang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>: Two domain-specific benchmarks tailored to evaluate GraphRAG performance on hierarchical retrieval and deep contextual understanding. The <span id="A6.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Medical</span> subset utilizes NCCN guidelines to test the handling of dense, rule-based clinical protocols, while the <span id="A6.p5.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Novel</span> subset employs literary texts from Gutenberg to assess the comprehension of implicit, non-linear narrative structures.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Implementation Details of Baselines</h2>

<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In our experiments, we compare our method against several widely used GraphRAG models.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">KGP</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2024</a>)</cite> facilitates multi-document question answering by constructing a graph where nodes represent passages or document structures. It employs an LLM-driven traversal agent to navigate semantic and structural connections, progressively aggregating supporting context for the final response.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">G-Retriever</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">He et al., 2024</a>)</cite> targets real-world textual graphs by formulating the subgraph retrieval task as a Prize-Collecting Steiner Tree (PCST) optimization problem. This approach extracts the most relevant subgraph to fit within the LLM context window, enabling effective conversational QA while mitigating hallucination and ensuring scalability.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RAPTOR</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sarthi et al., 2024</a>)</cite> employs a recursive abstraction approach to construct a hierarchical tree structure. By clustering and summarizing text chunks from the bottom up, it enables the retrieval of information at varying levels of granularity, capturing both high-level context and fine-grained details for holistic understanding.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MS-GraphRAG</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Edge et al., 2024</a>)</cite> enhances global corpus understanding by building an entity-relation graph and pre-computing community-level summaries. It answers queries by synthesizing insights from these communities, offering improved comprehensiveness for questions that span the entire document collection.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LazyGraphRAG</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Darren Edge, 2024</a>)</cite> introduces a cost-effective paradigm that eliminates the need for expensive up-front summarization of source data. By avoiding the pre-computation of community hierarchies, it reduces indexing costs to the level of standard vector RAG while maintaining superior performance on local queries and competitive quality on global queries compared to full-graph approaches.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LightRAG</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2024</a>)</cite> introduces a two-tier retrieval strategy designed to capture both detailed entity relationships and broader thematic contexts. It utilizes graph-enhanced indexing to facilitate rapid access to relevant information and allows for seamless integration of new data via an incremental update algorithm.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">HippoRAG</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gutiérrez et al., 2024</a>)</cite> proposes a neurobiologically inspired framework that orchestrates LLMs, knowledge graphs, and Personalized PageRank. It acts as a dual-system memory model to enable deep knowledge integration, facilitating robust retrieval for scenarios requiring the synthesis of information from multiple sources.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">HippoRAG2</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gutiérrez et al., 2025</a>)</cite> extends the Personalized PageRank-based framework of its predecessor by optimizing passage contextualization and the online interaction with LLMs. These enhancements enable the model to mimic human long-term memory more effectively, balancing robust factual recall with complex associative reasoning.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p10.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">E<sup id="A7.p10.1.1.1" class="ltx_sup">2</sup>GraphRAG</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al., 2025</a>)</cite> optimizes the GraphRAG paradigm by establishing bidirectional indexes between document chunks and entities. It combines a summary tree with a lightweight entity graph to facilitate fast lookup, enabling an adaptive retrieval process that seamlessly integrates local context and global understanding without manual query mode selection.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p11" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p11.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.p11.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">GFM-RAG</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Luo et al., 2025</a>)</cite> introduces a Graph Foundation Model (GFM) designed for zero-shot application on unseen datasets. It employs a pre-trained Graph Neural Network to reason over graph structures, effectively capturing complex query-knowledge relationships while mitigating the impact of noise and incompleteness in the constructed graphs.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p12" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p12.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.p12.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LogicRAG</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2025c</a>)</cite> introduces a dynamic retrieval paradigm where query-specific logic is modeled as a directed acyclic graph at inference time. By linearizing this graph via topological sort, it guides the retrieval process through a logically consistent sequence of sub-problems, significantly reducing token usage compared to static graph approaches.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p13" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p13.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.p13.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LinearRAG</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhuang et al., 2025</a>)</cite> challenges the reliance on costly and unstable relation extraction in existing methods. It constructs a relation-free hierarchical structure termed “Tri-Graph” using lightweight entity extraction and semantic linking. This approach scales linearly with corpus size and employs a two-stage retrieval strategy involving local entity activation and global importance aggregation.</p>
</div>
</section>
</article>
